target_customer: Apparel and footwear brands, multi-brand retailers and their suppliers that need carbon accounting, product lifecycle assessments and regulatory reporting
problem: Fashion brands could not measure emissions at product level or meet reporting rules because supplier data was scattered and carbon tools were generic.
product_category: Carbon management and environmental intelligence platform for fashion

founders.name: Marc Laurent
prior_employers: Kerala Ventures (co-founded seed VC firm at 25, per YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he invested 11 million euros across 16 seed startups including Doctolib, Malt and Playplay.

founders.name: Romain Champourlier
founders.background_notes: Described on the YC page as an entrepreneur and software engineer.

founders.name: Martin Daniel
previous_startups: Data For Good (volunteer data science community)

competitors.name: Plan A
competitors.what: Enterprise carbon accounting and ESG tracking software
competitors.funding_then: 10 million dollars raised six months after seed, November 2021 (a few months after the batch)

competitors.name: Sweep
competitors.funding_then: 5 million dollars round noted in 2021 coverage

technical_complexity.rationale: Product level lifecycle assessments need emission factor databases, supplier data pipelines and modelling, but this is data engineering rather than research.

defensibility.rationale: By 2026 it held 150,000 fashion emission factors and primary data from over 7,000 factories after buying Vaayu, which is hard to copy, though generic carbon tools were also competing.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Horizontal carbon platforms did not displace it; Carbonfact later bought Vaayu in May 2026.

market_need_then: Rising pressure from regulation and brand pledges on supply chain emissions, and VC investment in carbon accounting grew from 54.6 million dollars in 2020 to 398.5 million in 2021 per PitchBook cited by Axios.

branding.domain_note: Uses carbonfact.com; no acquisition history found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and outcome focused, stressing cutting time and cost and reducing emissions.

branding.brand_signature: Positioning as the first apparel and footwear carbon management platform
branding.community_and_virality: Vendor comparison pages against Sweep, Greenly, Plan A, Watershed and Normative; no consumer community or merch found.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear niche positioning with named brand customers such as Columbia and New Balance and wide trade press coverage of its funding and the Vaayu deal; no evidence of name driven growth.

outcome_analysis: Carbonfact picked fashion as a vertical for carbon accounting while horizontal rivals chased enterprises. It raised a 2 million dollar seed in June 2022 and a 15 million dollar Series A in April 2024, grew to 45 people and over 300 brands, and bought Vaayu in May 2026 to consolidate fashion product data. Regulation such as CSRD and Digital Product Passports added a tailwind.
notes: Seed amount is from Alven and Yahoo coverage (June 2022); Series A is stated by the company, EU-Startups, ESG Today and Finsmes (15 million dollars, about 13.9 million euros). Aggregators put total raised near 17 to 18 million dollars, consistent. Sweep source is the company's vendor comparison list only and the funding detail comes from a search snippet, so is loosely sourced. Education of founders not found. The Vaayu purchase on 2026-05-28 is an acquisition by Carbonfact, not an exit.
